declared_question: For a real small-molecule perturbation measured in two different real cell lines, how well does its transcriptional signature in one cell line predict its signature in the other, and does a naive comparison on absolute expression overstate that agreement?

source.title: L1000 Connectivity Map perturbational profiles from Broad Institute LINCS Center for Transcriptomics LINCS PHASE II
source.why_these_files: This series also ships a 2015-dated Level 2 release using simplified column labels (for example 'A375-trt_cp-5') that do not join to the current metadata files at all; verified directly by fetching it and finding zero of its column labels present in inst_info. Only the 2017-03-06 files, whose column IDs are real inst_id values, were used. The full 12,328-gene Level 4 (Z-score) and Level 5 (aggregated signature) releases for this series are 14 GB and 5.4 GB respectively, well outside this project's CPU-first scale; this protocol instead computes its own vehicle-control-relative differential signature from the 978-landmark-gene Level 2 data already cached, using only directly measured (not inferred) values.

entity.unit: one real small-molecule compound (pert_id) in one of the two fixed cell lines
entity.structure: canonical_smiles from GSE70138's own pert_info catalog, validated as RDKit-parseable; a literal 'restricted' or missing value is excluded, not treated as a valid structure

label_contract.raw_value: Level 2 (directly measured, deconvolved, 978 landmark genes) expression, one profile per instance well
label_contract.baseline_correction: each admitted compound-treated instance's profile has the median profile of every ctl_vehicle well on that exact same det_plate subtracted before aggregation; an instance whose plate has no vehicle-control well is excluded, not paired with a control from a different plate
label_contract.entity_aggregation: median, taken across an entity's replicate differential profiles after baseline correction, not before

comparison_contract.definition: For every compound admitted in both fixed cell lines, the Spearman correlation between its two 978-gene differential profiles.
comparison_contract.null_background: A single fixed, deterministic mismatch: the sorted shared-compound list rotated by one position, so each compound's cell-A profile is paired with a different, fixed compound's cell-B profile. This is one illustrative mismatched background, not a resampled null distribution, and uses no random state.
comparison_contract.significance_test: A two-sided Mann-Whitney U test between the matched and null Spearman-rho distributions.
comparison_contract.why_baseline_correction_is_declared_here: Computed once on raw Level 2 values with no correction, the matched-pair median rho was 0.79 against a null median of 0.70: both cell lines' raw profiles share enough baseline structure that even mismatched compound pairs correlate strongly. The vehicle-control subtraction this protocol requires exists specifically to remove that shared baseline before any correlation is computed.

excluded_by_design: any of the several thousand other real cell lines, doses, timepoints or perturbation types (shRNA, overexpression) this same GEO series also contains: this protocol fixes exactly two cell lines, one dose and one timepoint
the 11,350 computationally inferred genes outside the 978 directly measured landmark genes: this protocol uses only directly measured values
any claim that a cross-cell-line signature correlation predicts a clinical or in vivo outcome for any named compound
